nodes.rationale: Future autonomous runs have no access to the creating session, so the prompt must carry objective, steps, paths and success criteria itself.

Organization plugins take priority
nodes.rationale: Org-built plugins are tailored to the company's tools and workflows, so they outrank generic marketplace plugins.

nodes.label: Consent-first and no-PII guardrails
nodes.rationale: Only user-authored text is read, sample text is data not instructions, and the profile stores style patterns never personal values.

nodes.label: REVERSI Rule 1: test instruction only in modification
nodes.rationale: Using the instruction under test to also restore lets a systematic fault cancel itself out, so broken hardware would pass.

nodes.label: REVERSI Rule 2: handle information loss
nodes.rationale: Lossy instructions such as shift-left need control code to preserve bits; fully non-invertible ops (ABS, floating point rounding) defeat REVERSI.

nodes.label: Hazard/stall interaction bugs found by PATARA
100% coverage does not imply correctness
nodes.rationale: Coverage measures code that was written, so missing logic is invisible, errors can be masked, and REVERSI proves self-consistency rather than spec conformance.

nodes.label: Scope exclusions (CSRs, interrupts, privileged spec, RV32IM only)
Team 2: custom RISC-V processor with AI and vector extensions
Golden-model tension between PATARA and Vector Accelerator papers
nodes.rationale: PATARA reaches 100% code coverage without a reference model; the Vector Accelerator paper uses Spike and found 3,005 errors and taped out. High coverage and high bug yield are not the same thing.

Three comparison tensions (golden model, systematic vs random vs proof, scalability vs completeness)
